prerequisites: It is recommended to have completed the basic module courses Physics I and II and Mathematics I and II.

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge of the fundamentals of electronics.

Understand the electronic components commonly used in analog electronics, their behavior, characterization, and representation in electronic diagrams and schematics, as well as the practical limitations that must be considered in their use.
Understand the topology, structure, operation, and applications of the most common analog circuits.
Understand electronic and photonic devices and their application to solving engineering problems.
Become familiar with the technical language of analog electronics.
Understand the fundamentals of analyzing linear analog electronic systems, including the separation of AC and DC parts, and the calculation of currents, voltages, and powers.
Understand the principles of designing analog electronic circuits with discrete, integrated elements, and especially with operational amplifiers.
Understand basic computer simulation tools for electronic systems.
Become familiar with the scientific method in circuit analysis and design.
Understand traditional and digital information sources related to electronics.
Recognize, analyze, design, simulate, assemble, and verify, through direct measurements, analog circuits of basic and medium complexity.
Prepare individual and group works, developing critical capacity to discuss results and compare experimental conclusions with theoretical knowledge.
Perform supervised laboratory practices, analyze collected data, and prepare lab reports.
Use basic laboratory equipment (oscilloscopes, power supplies, multimeters, signal generators, assembly systems).
Solve practical and theoretical problems related to electronic systems.
Design analog circuits, including the use of operational amplifiers.
Work collaboratively in small groups to carry out practices and projects.
Integrate knowledge and skills in the development of practical electronics projects.

syllabus_topics: Practice 1. Introduction to Simulation and Laboratory (not graded).
teaching_methods: Online documentation for consultation in the form of learning modules, previously prepared by the department.
Execution of practical exercises with physical assembly in the laboratory under a Flipped Learning model.
Individual study of the theoretical content of each topic.
Assimilation of knowledge derived from topics taught in theoretical classes.
Active participation in solving exercises proposed in lectures.
Comprehensive reading of provided material for the acquisition of practical concepts.
Monitoring and completion of proposed activities prior to the laboratory session (group activities).
Assembly and measurements during laboratory sessions (group activities).

assessment_methods.method: Active participation (in-class problem solving and homework submission)
Practical content in small groups (conceptual practice evaluation test, circuit assembly evaluation, individual and group practical activities)

assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, the final grade is calculated as 30% from practices, 60% from theoretical exams, and 10% from active participation. Students must score over 5/10 in each theoretical exam topic and achieve a practical grade of 60% or higher to pass. Failing to obtain at least 25% of practical points or successfully completing a minimum of three lab activities results in a 0 for the practical part. In the extraordinary call, students re-evaluate unpassed practicals and theoretical components. For unique evaluation, the final grade is 30% from practices and 70% from a theoretical-practical exam.
